answer: Every few hours the network sends each identity an unannounced puzzle taking about twenty seconds of computation, due within ninety seconds. The puzzles go out to everyone at the same moment, so one operator steering a hundred accounts would need a hundred machines solving at once, not one script taking turns. Miss twice in an epoch and earnings freeze while a 50-credit bond burns. The nectar here is steady work, not a shortcut: a grove of watchers issues the puzzles and keeps an atlas of who answered on time, so slow or copied answers stand out at once.
